title.zh: 卷二十六 列傳第二十 范岫 傅昭 弟映 蕭琛 陸杲
title.en: Volume 26: Fan Xiu; Fu Zhao; Fu Ying; Xiao Chen; Lu Gao
title.raw: 卷二十六 列傳第二十 范岫 傅昭 弟映 蕭琛 陸杲 Volume 26: Fan Xiu; Fu Zhao; Fu Ying; Xiao Chen; Lu Gao

sentences.zh: 梁書卷第二十六 列傳第二十

translations.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 26, Biographies 20
translations.idiomatic: Book of Liang, Volume 26, Biographies, Number 20

sentences.zh: 范岫 傅昭 弟映 蕭琛 陸杲

translations.literal: Fan Xiu; Fu Zhao; younger brother Ying; Xiao Chen; Lu Gao
translations.idiomatic: Fan Xiu; Fu Zhao; his younger brother Ying; Xiao Chen; and Lu Gao

sentences.zh: 范岫字懋賓，濟陽考城人也。

translations.literal: Fan Xiu, courtesy name Maobin, was a native of Kaocheng in Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Xiu, styled Maobin, came from Kaocheng in Jiyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 高祖宣，晉徵士。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Xuan was a reclusive scholar of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Xuan had been a Jin dynasty recluse-scholar.

sentences.zh: 父羲，宋兗州別駕。

translations.literal: His father Yi was an aide of Yanzhou in Song.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yi had served as chief aide to the governor of Yan Province under the Song.

sentences.zh: 岫早孤，事母以孝聞，與吳興沈約俱爲蔡興宗所禮。

translations.literal: Xiu lost his father early; he was famed for filial service to his mother, and he and Shen Yue of Wuxing were both honored by Cai Xingzong.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu was orphaned young but won renown for tending his mother with filial devotion; he and Shen Yue of Wuxing were alike held in esteem by Cai Xingzong.

sentences.zh: 泰始中，起家奉朝請。

translations.literal: In the Taishi era he first entered office as a court attendant.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taishi reign he began his career as a palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 興宗爲安西將軍，引爲主簿。

translations.literal: When Xingzong became General Who Pacifies the West, he took Xiu on as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Xingzong was appointed General Who Pacifies the West, he brought Xiu in as his chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 累遷臨海、長城二縣令，驃騎參軍，尚書刪定郎，護軍司馬，齊司徒竟陵王子良記室參軍。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to magistrate of Linhai and Changcheng counties, staff officer to the Rapid Cavalry General, revising clerk in the Ministry of Works, army aide to the Protector-General, and recorder on the staff of Prince Ziliang of Jingling, Grand Tutor of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through a series of posts: magistrate of Linhai and Changcheng, staff officer to the Rapid Cavalry General, revising clerk in the Ministry of Works, army aide to the Protector-General, and recorder on the staff of Qi’s Grand Tutor, Prince Ziliang of Jingling.

sentences.zh: 累遷太子家令。

translations.literal: He was further promoted to Director of the Heir Apparent’s Household.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to Director of the Heir Apparent’s Household.

sentences.zh: 文惠太子之在東宮，沈約之徒以文才見引，岫亦預焉。

translations.literal: While the Literary and Gracious Heir Apparent was in the Eastern Palace, Shen Yue and his circle were drawn in for literary talent, and Xiu was among them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Literary and Gracious Heir Apparent resided in the Eastern Palace, Shen Yue and others were recruited for their literary gifts, and Xiu was included among them.

sentences.zh: 岫文雖不逮約，而名行爲時輩所與，博涉多通，尤悉魏晉以來吉凶故事。

translations.literal: Though Xiu’s writing did not match Yue’s, his reputation and conduct were acknowledged by contemporaries; he was broadly learned and especially versed in auspicious and inauspicious precedents from Wei and Jin onward.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu’s prose did not equal Yue’s, yet contemporaries respected his name and conduct; widely read and well informed, he was above all expert in ritual and omens from Wei and Jin times onward.

sentences.zh: 約常稱曰：「范公好事該博，胡廣無以加。

translations.literal: Yue often said, “Master Fan is fond of learning and thoroughly informed; even Hu Guang could not surpass him.
translations.idiomatic: Yue would often remark, “Master Fan delights in inquiry and knows everything—Hu Guang himself could add nothing.

sentences.zh: 」南鄉范雲謂人曰：「諸君進止威儀，當問范長頭。

translations.literal: ” Fan Yun of Nanxiang told others, “Gentlemen, for questions of deportment and ritual bearing, you should ask Long-Head Fan.
translations.idiomatic: ” Fan Yun of Nanxiang told people, “For how to advance, withdraw, and comport yourselves, ask Long-Head Fan.

sentences.zh: 」以岫多識前代舊事也。

translations.literal: ” This was because Xiu knew so many stories of former ages.
translations.idiomatic: ” — for Xiu knew the old precedents of earlier dynasties better than anyone.

sentences.zh: 遷國子博士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Erudite of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Erudite of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 永明中，魏使至，有詔妙選朝士有詞辯者，接使於界首，以岫兼淮陰長史迎焉。

translations.literal: In the Yongming era a Wei envoy arrived; an edict called for the finest court gentlemen skilled in debate to receive the envoy at the border, and Xiu was appointed acting chief clerk of Huaiyin to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongming an envoy from Wei arrived; the court was ordered to choose the most articulate officials to meet him at the frontier, and Xiu was sent as acting chief clerk of Huaiyin to receive him.

sentences.zh: 還遷尚書左丞，母憂去官，尋起攝職。

translations.literal: On his return he was promoted to Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs; he left office for his mother’s mourning, then soon resumed duties in an acting capacity.
translations.idiomatic: After returning he was made Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs; he resigned on his mother’s death but soon took up his duties again in an acting post.

sentences.zh: 出爲寧朔將軍、南蠻長史、南義陽太守，未赴職，遷右軍諮議參軍，郡如故。

translations.literal: He went out as General Who Pacifies the North, chief clerk of the Southern Man, and Administrator of Southern Yiyang; before he took up the post he was transferred to staff adviser of the Right Army, while retaining his commandery title.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as General Who Pacifies the North, chief clerk of the Southern Man, and administrator of Southern Yiyang; before he assumed the post he was made staff adviser of the Right Army, retaining his nominal commandery rank.

sentences.zh: 除撫軍司馬。

translations.literal: He was appointed army aide to the Pacification General.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed army aide to the Pacification General.

sentences.zh: 出爲建威將軍、安成內史。

translations.literal: He went out as General Who Establishes Might and Interior Secretary of Ancheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as General Who Establishes Might and interior secretary of Ancheng.

sentences.zh: 入爲給事黃門侍郎，遷御史中丞、領前軍將軍、南北兗二州大中正。

translations.literal: He entered service as Attendant Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, then was transferred to Censor-in-Chief, concurrently commanding the Vanguard General and serving as chief arbiter of pedigree for both northern and southern Yan provinces.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as Attendant Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, then became Censor-in-Chief, concurrently commanding the Vanguard General and serving as chief arbiter of pedigree for northern and southern Yan.

sentences.zh: 永元末，出爲輔國將軍、冠軍晉安王長史，行南徐州事。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongyuan he went out as General Who Assists the State and chief clerk to the Champion Prince of Jin’an, acting for the southern Xu region.
translations.idiomatic: At the close of Yongyuan he was sent out as General Who Assists the State and chief clerk to the Champion Prince of Jin’an, with charge of southern Xu.

sentences.zh: 義師平京邑，承制徵爲尚書吏部郎，參大選。

translations.literal: When the righteous army pacified the capital, he was summoned by provisional order to be Director of the Ministry of Personnel and took part in the great selection.
translations.idiomatic: After the righteous army took the capital, he was summoned under provisional authority to be Director of the Ministry of Personnel and took part in the great appointments.

sentences.zh: 梁臺建，爲度支尚書。

translations.literal: When the Liang headquarters was established, he became Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang provisional government was set up, he became Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 天監五年，遷散騎常侍、光祿大夫，侍皇太子，給扶。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianjian he was transferred to Regular Attendant and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, attending the crown prince with a staff granted.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjian year 5 he was made Regular Attendant and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, attending the crown prince with a ceremonial staff.

sentences.zh: 六年，領太子左衛率。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he concurrently held the post of Left Commandant of the Crown Prince’s Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 he also served as Left Commandant of the Crown Prince’s Guard.

sentences.zh: 七年，徙通直散騎常侍、右衛將軍，中正如故。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was moved to Regular Attendant of Direct Communication and General of the Right Guard, retaining his post as chief arbiter.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 he was transferred to Regular Attendant of Direct Communication and General of the Right Guard, keeping his arbiter’s post.

sentences.zh: 其年表致事，詔不許。

translations.literal: That year he memorialized to retire; the edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he petitioned to retire; the throne refused.

sentences.zh: 八年，出爲晉陵太守，秩中二千石。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he went out as Administrator of Jinling, with rank of two thousand bushels.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 he was sent out as administrator of Jinling, at the two-thousand-bushel rank.

sentences.zh: 九年，入爲祠部尚書，領右驍騎將軍，其年遷金紫光祿大夫，加親信二十人。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he entered as Minister of Rites, concurrently commanding the Right Valiant Cavalry General; that year he was transferred to Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, with twenty personal attendants added.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9 he returned as Minister of Rites and concurrently commanded the Right Valiant Cavalry General; that year he was promoted to Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon with twenty personal attendants.

sentences.zh: 十三年，卒官，時年七十五。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he died in office at the age of seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: In year 13 he died in office, aged seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 賻錢五萬，布百匹。

translations.literal: Funeral gifts were fifty thousand cash and a hundred bolts of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted fifty thousand cash and a hundred bolts of cloth for his funeral.

sentences.zh: 岫身長七尺八寸，恭敬儼恪，進止以禮。

translations.literal: Xiu stood seven feet eight inches tall, reverent and dignified in bearing, advancing and withdrawing according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu stood seven feet eight inches in height, grave and courteous in manner, every step governed by ritual.

sentences.zh: 自親喪之後，蔬食布衣以終身。

translations.literal: After his parents’ mourning he ate vegetables and wore plain cloth for the rest of his life.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his parents he ate only plain food and wore coarse cloth for the rest of his days.

sentences.zh: 每所居官，恒以廉潔著稱。

translations.literal: In every office he held he was constantly famed for integrity and purity.
translations.idiomatic: In every post he held he was known for incorruptible conduct.

sentences.zh: 爲長城令時，有梓材巾箱，至數十年，經貴遂不改易。

translations.literal: When he was magistrate of Changcheng he had a catalpa-wood cap-box; for several decades, though he rose in rank, he never replaced it.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Changcheng he kept a catalpa-wood cap-box; for decades, even after he rose to high office, he never replaced it.

sentences.zh: 在晉陵，惟作牙管筆一雙，猶以爲費。

translations.literal: At Jinling he had made only one pair of ivory-barrel brushes, and even that he regarded as extravagant.
translations.idiomatic: At Jinling he allowed himself only one pair of ivory-barrel writing brushes—and even that he thought excessive.

sentences.zh: 所著文集、《禮論》、《雜儀》、《字訓》行於世。

translations.literal: His collected writings, Treatise on Rites, Miscellaneous Ritual Protocols, and Character Instruction circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings, Treatise on Rites, Miscellaneous Ritual Protocols, and Character Instruction circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 二子褒，偉。

translations.literal: He had two sons, Bao and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He left two sons, Bao and Wei.

sentences.zh: 傅昭，字茂遠，北地靈州人，晉司隸校尉咸七世孫也。

translations.literal: Fu Zhao, courtesy name Maoyuan, was a native of Lingzhou in Beidi, seventh-generation descendant of Fu Xian, Director of the Metropolitan Area under Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zhao, styled Maoyuan, came from Lingzhou in Beidi—seventh in descent from Jin’s Director of the Metropolitan Area, Fu Xian.

sentences.zh: 祖和之，父淡，善《三禮》，知名宋世。

translations.literal: His grandfather was Hezhi; his father Dan was skilled in the Three Rites and famed in the Song era.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather was Hezhi; his father Dan mastered the Three Rites and was renowned in Song times.

sentences.zh: 淡事宋竟陵王劉誕，誕反，淡坐誅。

translations.literal: Dan served Prince Jingling of Song, Liu Dan; when Dan rebelled, Dan was executed for the crime.
translations.idiomatic: Dan had served Prince Jingling of Song, Liu Dan; when the prince rebelled, Dan was executed as an accomplice.

sentences.zh: 昭六歲而孤，哀毀如成人者，宗黨咸異之。

translations.literal: Zhao was orphaned at six; his grief and self-mortification were like an adult’s, and the whole clan marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao lost his father at six; his mourning was as deep as a grown man’s, and the whole clan wondered at him.

sentences.zh: 十一，隨外祖於朱雀航賣曆日。

translations.literal: At eleven he followed his maternal grandfather to sell almanacs at the Zhuque ferry.
translations.idiomatic: At eleven he helped his maternal grandfather sell almanacs at the Zhuque ferry.

sentences.zh: 爲雍州刺史袁顗客，顗嘗來昭所，昭讀書自若，神色不改。

translations.literal: He was a retainer of Yuan Yi, Governor of Yong Province; Yi once came to Zhao’s place, and Zhao read on as before without change of expression.
translations.idiomatic: He was retained by Yuan Yi, governor of Yong Province; when Yi once visited Zhao’s lodging, Zhao went on reading without a change of expression.

sentences.zh: 顗歎曰：「此兒神情不凡，必成佳器。

translations.literal: Yi sighed and said, “This boy’s spirit and bearing are extraordinary; he is sure to become a fine vessel.
translations.idiomatic: Yi sighed and said, “This boy’s spirit is uncommon—he will surely become someone of note.

sentences.zh: 」司徒建安王休仁聞而悅之，因欲致昭，昭以宋氏多故，遂不往。

translations.literal: ” Prince Jian’an, the Grand Tutor Xiu Ren, heard of this and was pleased; he wished to summon Zhao, but Zhao, because the Song house was beset by troubles, did not go.
translations.idiomatic: ” Grand Tutor Xiu Ren, Prince of Jian’an, heard of this and was delighted; he wished to bring Zhao in, but Zhao, citing the Song court’s turmoil, declined to go.

sentences.zh: 或有稱昭於廷尉虞愿，愿乃遣車迎昭。

translations.literal: Someone praised Zhao to Yu Yuan, Director of Justice; Yuan then sent a carriage to welcome Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Someone commended Zhao to Yu Yuan, the Director of Justice, and Yuan sent a carriage to fetch him.

sentences.zh: 時愿宗人通之在坐，並當世名流，通之贈昭詩曰：「英妙擅山東，才子傾洛陽。

translations.literal: At the time Yuan’s clansman Tongzhi was present, both men being celebrated figures of the age; Tongzhi presented Zhao with a poem saying, “Outstanding talent excels east of the mountains; a young genius turns heads in Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan’s kinsman Tongzhi was also present—both were luminaries of the day—and Tongzhi gave Zhao a poem: “A prodigy famed east of the mountains, a young talent who turns Luoyang’s head.

sentences.zh: 清塵誰能嗣，及爾遘遺芳。

translations.literal: Who can inherit such pure renown? Meeting you, I encounter a lingering fragrance.
translations.idiomatic: Who could inherit such pure renown? In meeting you I find a fragrance that endures.

sentences.zh: 」太原王延秀薦昭於丹陽尹袁粲，深爲所禮，辟爲郡主簿，使諸子從昭受學。

translations.literal: ” Wang Yanxiu of Taiyuan recommended Zhao to Yuan Can, Governor of Danyang, who honored him deeply, appointed him chief clerk of the commandery, and had his sons study under Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: ” Wang Yanxiu of Taiyuan recommended Zhao to Yuan Can, governor of Danyang, who treated him with great respect, made him chief clerk of the commandery, and had his sons study under him.

sentences.zh: 會明帝崩，粲造哀策文，乃引昭定其所制。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming died, Can composed the mourning proclamation and brought Zhao in to fix what he had drafted.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming died, Can drafted the mourning proclamation and had Zhao revise it.

sentences.zh: 每經昭戶，輒歎曰：「經其戶，寂若無人，披其帷，其人斯在，豈非名賢！

translations.literal: Whenever he passed Zhao’s door he would sigh and say, “Passing his gate it is silent as if no one were there; drawing aside the curtain, the man is there—surely a famed worthy!
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he passed Zhao’s door he would sigh: “At his gate all is still as though no one were within; yet draw the curtain and the man is there—is this not a true sage?

sentences.zh: 」尋爲總明學士、奉朝請。

translations.literal: ” Soon Zhao became a scholar of the Zongming Hall and a court attendant.
translations.idiomatic: ” Soon after he became a scholar of the Zongming Hall and a court attendant.

sentences.zh: 齊永明中，累遷員外郎、司徒竟陵王子良參軍、尚書儀曹郎。

translations.literal: In Qi’s Yongming era he was promoted in succession to outer court gentleman, staff officer to the Grand Tutor Prince Ziliang of Jingling, and clerk in the Ministry of Rites’ Ceremonial Section.
translations.idiomatic: During Qi’s Yongming reign he rose through outer court gentleman, staff officer to Grand Tutor Prince Ziliang of Jingling, and clerk in the Ceremonial Section of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 先是御史中丞劉休薦昭於武帝，永明初，以昭爲南郡王侍讀。

translations.literal: Earlier the Censor-in-Chief Liu Xiu had recommended Zhao to Emperor Wu; at the beginning of Yongming Zhao was made tutor to the Prince of Nanjun.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Censor-in-Chief Liu Xiu had recommended Zhao to Emperor Wu; at the start of Yongming he was made tutor to the Prince of Nanjun.

sentences.zh: 王嗣帝位，故時臣隸爭求權寵，惟昭及南陽宗夬，保身守正，無所參入，竟不罹其禍。

translations.literal: When the prince succeeded to the throne, former retainers scrambled for power and favor; only Zhao and Zong Que of Nanyang kept themselves upright and took no part, and in the end they did not suffer the calamity.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince ascended the throne, former retainers fought for favor and power; only Zhao and Zong Que of Nanyang kept their integrity and stayed aloof, and in the end they escaped the purge.

sentences.zh: 明帝踐阼，引昭爲中書通事舍人。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming took the throne he brought Zhao in as Secretariat Attendant for Current Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming acceded, he brought Zhao in as Secretariat Attendant for Current Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時居此職者，皆勢傾天下，昭獨廉靜，無所干豫。

translations.literal: Those who held this post at the time all bent the world to their power; Zhao alone was pure and quiet, meddling in nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Others in that office wielded power over the realm; Zhao alone remained incorrupt and withdrawn, interfering in nothing.

sentences.zh: 器服率陋，身安粗糲。

translations.literal: His implements and dress were plain and shabby; he was content with coarse fare.
translations.idiomatic: His furnishings and dress were plain; he was content with coarse food.

sentences.zh: 常插燭於板床，明帝聞之，賜漆合燭盤等，敕曰：「卿有古人之風，故賜卿古人之物。

translations.literal: He would often stick a candle into a plank bed; when Emperor Ming heard of this he granted him a lacquered candle box and tray, with an order saying, “You have the manner of the ancients, so I grant you the things of the ancients.
translations.idiomatic: He would stick a candle into a plank bed; when Emperor Ming heard of it he sent a lacquered candle box and tray, writing: “You have the spirit of the ancients, so I give you the furnishings of the ancients.

sentences.zh: 」累遷車騎臨海王記室參軍，長水校尉，太子家令，驃騎晉安王諮議參軍。

translations.literal: ” He was promoted in succession to recorder on the staff of the Cavalry General Prince of Linhai, Commandant of the Changshui Guard, Director of the Heir Apparent’s Household, and staff adviser to the Rapid Cavalry Prince of Jin’an.
translations.idiomatic: ” He rose through recorder to the Cavalry General Prince of Linhai, Commandant of the Changshui Guard, Director of the Heir Apparent’s Household, and staff adviser to the Rapid Cavalry Prince of Jin’an.

sentences.zh: 尋除尚書左丞、本州大中正。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs and chief arbiter of his native province.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs and chief arbiter of his home province.

sentences.zh: 高祖素悉昭能，建康城平，引爲驃騎錄事參軍。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor had long known Zhao’s ability; when Jiankang was pacified he brought him in as recording officer on the staff of the Rapid Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: The High Ancestor had long known Zhao’s gifts; when Jiankang fell he brought him in as recording officer on the Rapid Cavalry staff.

sentences.zh: 梁臺建，遷給事黃門侍郎，領著作郎，頃之，兼御史中丞，黃門、著作、中正並如故。

translations.literal: When the Liang headquarters was established he was transferred to Attendant Gentleman at the Yellow Gate and concurrently Director of the History Office; soon after he also served as Censor-in-Chief, retaining his posts at the Yellow Gate, the History Office, and as chief arbiter.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang provisional government was set up he became Attendant Gentleman at the Yellow Gate and Director of the History Office; soon he also served as Censor-in-Chief while keeping his Yellow Gate, History Office, and arbiter posts.

sentences.zh: 天監三年，兼五兵尚書，參選事，四年，卽真。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianjian he concurrently held the post of Minister of the Five Arms and took part in selections; in the fourth year he received the full appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjian year 3 he also served as Minister of the Five Arms and took part in appointments; in year 4 he received the full title.

sentences.zh: 六年，徙爲左民尚書，未拜，出爲建威將軍、平南安成王長史、尋陽太守。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was moved to Minister of the Left People; before he received the seal he went out as General Who Establishes Might, chief clerk to the Pacification Prince of Ancheng, and Administrator of Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 he was transferred to Minister of the Left People; before taking the seal he was sent out as General Who Establishes Might, chief clerk to the Pacification Prince of Ancheng, and administrator of Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 七年，入爲振遠將軍、中權長史。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he entered as General Who Quells the Distance and chief clerk of the Central Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 he returned as General Who Quells the Distance and chief clerk of the Central Guard.

sentences.zh: 八年，遷通直散騎常侍，領步兵校尉，復領本州大中正。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to Regular Attendant of Direct Communication, concurrently Commandant of the Footsoldiers, and again held the chief arbiter’s post for his native province.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 he became Regular Attendant of Direct Communication and Commandant of the Footsoldiers, resuming his post as chief arbiter of his home province.

sentences.zh: 十年，復爲左民尚書。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he again became Minister of the Left People.
translations.idiomatic: In year 10 he again became Minister of the Left People.

sentences.zh: 十一年，出爲信武將軍、安成內史。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he went out as Trustworthy Martial General and Interior Secretary of Ancheng.
translations.idiomatic: In year 11 he was sent out as Trustworthy Martial General and interior secretary of Ancheng.

sentences.zh: 安成自宋已來兵亂，郡舍號凶。

translations.literal: Since Song times Ancheng had suffered military turmoil, and the prefectural residence was called ill-omened.
translations.idiomatic: Since Song times Ancheng had been ravaged by war, and the prefectural residence was considered haunted.

sentences.zh: 及昭爲郡，郡內人夜夢見兵馬鎧甲甚盛，又聞有人云「當避善人」，軍衆相與騰虛而逝。

translations.literal: When Zhao became administrator, a man in the commandery dreamed at night of armored troops in great array, and heard someone say, “We must yield to the good man”; the soldiers all rose into the air together and departed.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao took the commandery, a local man dreamed one night of armored hosts in full array and heard a voice say, “Make way for the good man”; the soldiers all rose into the air and vanished together.

sentences.zh: 夢者驚起。

translations.literal: The dreamer started awake.
translations.idiomatic: The dreamer woke with a start.

sentences.zh: 俄而疾風暴雨，倏忽便至，數間屋俱倒，卽夢者所見軍馬踐蹈之所也。

translations.literal: Presently a violent wind and torrential rain came in an instant; several rooms collapsed together—the very ground where the dreamer had seen the army and horses trample.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a fierce wind and driving rain struck without warning; several buildings collapsed on the very spot where, in the dream, the army had trodden.

sentences.zh: 自後郡舍遂安，咸以昭正直所致。

translations.literal: From then on the prefectural residence was at peace; all attributed it to Zhao’s uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: After that the residence was untroubled; everyone credited Zhao’s integrity.

sentences.zh: 郡溪無魚，或有暑月薦昭魚者，昭旣不納，又不欲拒，遂餧于門側。

translations.literal: The commandery streams had no fish; in the hot months someone once presented fish to Zhao. Zhao would neither accept them nor outright refuse, and so he fed them at the side of his gate.
translations.idiomatic: The streams of the commandery held no fish; one summer someone offered Zhao fish. He would neither accept nor refuse outright, and so he fed them beside his gate.

sentences.zh: 十二年，入爲秘書監，領後軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he entered as Director of the Secretariat and concurrently commanded the Rear Army General.
translations.idiomatic: In year 12 he returned as Director of the Secretariat and concurrently commanded the Rear Army General.

sentences.zh: 十四年，遷太常卿。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was transferred to Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: In year 14 he was made Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 十七年，出爲智武將軍、臨海太守。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he went out as Sagacious Martial General and Administrator of Linhai.
translations.idiomatic: In year 17 he was sent out as Sagacious Martial General and administrator of Linhai.

sentences.zh: 郡有蜜巖，前後太守皆自封固，專收其利。

translations.literal: The commandery had a honey cliff; former and later administrators all sealed it off for themselves and monopolized its profits.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery had a honey cliff; successive administrators had sealed it off and kept the profits for themselves.

sentences.zh: 昭以周文之囿，與百姓共之，大可喻小，乃教勿封。

translations.literal: Zhao reasoned that King Wen’s park was shared with the people—the large can illustrate the small—and so he ordered that it not be sealed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao cited King Wen’s park, shared with the people—the great can stand for the small—and ordered that it remain open.

sentences.zh: 縣令常餉栗，置絹于薄下，昭笑而還之。

translations.literal: The county magistrate often sent chestnuts as tribute, placing silk beneath the covering; Zhao smiled and returned them.
translations.idiomatic: The county magistrate often sent chestnuts with silk hidden beneath the wrapping; Zhao smiled and sent them back.

sentences.zh: 普通二年，入爲通直散騎常侍、光祿大夫，領本州大中正，尋領秘書監。

translations.literal: In the second year of Putong he entered as Regular Attendant of Direct Communication and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, concurrently chief arbiter of his native province; soon he also held the Directorate of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Putong year 2 he returned as Regular Attendant of Direct Communication and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, chief arbiter of his home province; soon he also directed the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 五年，遷散騎常侍、金紫光祿大夫，中正如故。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to Regular Attendant and Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, retaining his post as chief arbiter.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he was made Regular Attendant and Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, keeping his arbiter’s post.

sentences.zh: 昭所蒞官，常以清靜爲政，不尚嚴肅。

translations.literal: In every office Zhao held he governed by quiet purity and did not prize severity.
translations.idiomatic: In every post he held Zhao governed through quiet integrity rather than harsh severity.

sentences.zh: 居朝廷，無所請謁，不畜私門生，不交私利。

translations.literal: At court he made no requests or visits, kept no private disciples, and entered into no private profit.
translations.idiomatic: At court he made no solicitations, kept no private disciples, and took no illicit gain.

sentences.zh: 終日端居，以書記爲樂，雖老不衰。

translations.literal: He sat upright all day, taking joy in writing and record-keeping, and even in old age did not flag.
translations.idiomatic: He sat in quiet study all day, finding his pleasure in books and records, and did not slacken even in old age.

sentences.zh: 博極古今，尤善人物，魏晉以來，官宦簿伐，姻通內外，舉而論之，無所遺失。

translations.literal: He was exhaustively learned in past and present and especially skilled in persons; from Wei and Jin onward, official registers, pedigree, and marriage ties within and without—discussing them all, he omitted nothing.
translations.idiomatic: His learning spanned antiquity and his own age; above all he knew people—from Wei and Jin on, office lists, pedigrees, and marriage alliances inside and out—and could discourse on them without omission.

sentences.zh: 性尤篤慎。

translations.literal: His nature was especially sincere and cautious.
translations.idiomatic: His character was profoundly conscientious.

sentences.zh: 子婦嘗得家餉牛肉以進，昭召其子曰：「食之則犯法，告之則不可，取而埋之。

translations.literal: His daughter-in-law once received beef sent from her family and presented it; Zhao summoned his son and said, “To eat it would violate the law; to report it would be impossible—take it and bury it.
translations.idiomatic: His daughter-in-law once received beef from her family and served it to him; Zhao called his son and said, “To eat it breaks the law; to report it is impossible—take it and bury it.

sentences.zh: 」其居身行己，不負闇室，類皆如此。

translations.literal: ” In how he conducted himself in private he did not betray the dark room; his conduct was all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: ” In private conduct he would not compromise even where no one could see; nearly everything he did was of this sort.

sentences.zh: 京師後進，宗其學，重其道，人人自以爲不逮。

translations.literal: The younger generation in the capital revered his learning and honored his way; each felt himself unequal to Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Young scholars in the capital revered his learning and honored his path; each felt himself unable to match him.

sentences.zh: 大通二年九月，卒，時年七十五。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the second year of Datong he died at the age of seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Datong year 2 he died, aged seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 詔賻錢三萬，布五十匹，卽日舉哀，諡曰貞子。

translations.literal: An edict granted thirty thousand cash and fifty bolts of cloth for his funeral; mourning was observed that same day; his posthumous title was Zhenzi.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted thirty thousand cash and fifty bolts of cloth; mourning was proclaimed that day; his posthumous title was Zhenzi, “the Upright.”

sentences.zh: 長子諝，尚書郎，臨安令。

translations.literal: His eldest son Xu was a gentleman of the Ministry of Works and magistrate of Lin’an.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Xu served as a gentleman of the Ministry of Works and as magistrate of Lin’an.

sentences.zh: 次子肱。

translations.literal: His second son was Gong.
translations.idiomatic: His second son was Gong.

sentences.zh: 映字徽遠，昭弟也。

translations.literal: Ying, courtesy name Huiyuan, was Zhao’s younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Ying, styled Huiyuan, was Zhao’s younger brother.

sentences.zh: 三歲而孤。

translations.literal: He was orphaned at three.
translations.idiomatic: He was orphaned at the age of three.

sentences.zh: 兄弟友睦，修身厲行，非禮不行。

translations.literal: The brothers were friendly and harmonious, cultivating the person and strict in conduct; what was not ritual they would not do.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers lived in warm accord, disciplined in conduct and strict in observance; nothing contrary to ritual was permitted.

sentences.zh: 始昭之守臨海，陸倕餞之，賓主俱歡，日昏不反，映以昭年高，不可連夜極樂，乃自往迎候，同乘而歸，兄弟並已斑白，時人美而服焉。

translations.literal: When Zhao first became administrator of Linhai, Lu Chun gave him a farewell feast; host and guests were all merry, and at dusk he did not return. Ying thought that Zhao, being advanced in years, ought not to revel through the night to excess, and so went himself to meet him; they rode back together. Both brothers’ hair was already streaked with white, and people of the time admired and submitted to this.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao first took office at Linhai, Lu Chun gave him a farewell feast; host and guests made merry until dusk, and Zhao did not return. Ying thought his elder brother, at his age, should not carouse all night; he went to fetch him himself, and they rode home together—both already gray-haired. Contemporaries admired and revered the deed.

sentences.zh: 及昭卒，映喪之如父，年逾七十，哀戚過禮，服制雖除，每言輒感慟。

translations.literal: When Zhao died, Ying mourned him as for a father; though past seventy, his grief exceeded the rites; though the mourning garments were laid aside, whenever he spoke he was moved to sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao died, Ying mourned him as a father; though over seventy, his grief exceeded the prescribed rites, and even after the mourning period ended, speech would still move him to tears.

sentences.zh: 映泛涉記傳，有文才，而不以篇什自命。

translations.literal: Ying read widely in histories and chronicles, possessed literary talent, yet did not style himself a poet.
translations.idiomatic: Ying read widely in histories and chronicles and had literary gifts, yet he did not claim the name of poet.

sentences.zh: 少時與劉繪、蕭琛相友善，繪之爲南康相，映時爲府丞，文教多令具草。

translations.literal: In youth he was close friends with Liu Hui and Xiao Chen; when Hui became Administrator of Nankang, Ying was at the time a commandery aide, and for many documents of culture and instruction Hui had him draft them.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was close to Liu Hui and Xiao Chen; when Hui became administrator of Nankang and Ying served as his commandery aide, Hui often had him draft official documents.

sentences.zh: 褚彥回聞而悅之，乃屈與子賁等遊處。

translations.literal: Chu Yanhui heard of this and was pleased; he then condescended to let him associate with his son Ben and others.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Yanhui heard of him with pleasure and allowed him to keep company with his son Ben and the like.

sentences.zh: 年未弱冠，彥回欲令仕，映以昭未解褐，固辭，須昭仕乃官。

translations.literal: Before he had reached twenty, Yanhui wished to have him enter office; Ying, because Zhao had not yet taken up the official robe, firmly declined, saying he must wait until Zhao took office before he himself would serve.
translations.idiomatic: Before he was twenty Yanhui wished him to take office, but Ying refused firmly while Zhao had not yet entered service; he would not take rank until his brother did.

sentences.zh: 永元元年，參鎮軍江夏王軍事，出爲武康令。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongyuan he served on the staff of the Pacification General, Prince of Jiangxia, and went out as magistrate of Wukang.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongyuan year 1 he served on the staff of the Pacification General, Prince of Jiangxia, and was sent out as magistrate of Wukang.

sentences.zh: 及高祖師次建康，吳興太守袁昂自謂門世忠貞，固守誠節，乃訪於映曰：「卿謂時事云何？

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor’s army halted at Jiankang, Yuan Ang, Administrator of Wuxing, considering his family loyal through generations, held fast to sincere constancy, and so consulted Ying, saying, “What do you think of the present situation?
translations.idiomatic: When the High Ancestor’s army reached Jiankang, Yuan Ang, administrator of Wuxing, believing his house loyal through generations, clung to his oath of fealty and asked Ying, “What do you make of the times?

sentences.zh: 」映答曰：「元嘉之末，開闢未有，故太尉殺身以明節，司徒當寄託之重，理無苟全，所以不顧夷險，以殉名義。

translations.literal: ” Ying answered, “At the end of Yuanjia the mandate was not yet settled, and so the Grand Marshal gave his life to clarify integrity; the Minister over the Masses bore the weight of entrustment—reason allowed no selfish preservation—hence he did not regard hardship or ease and died for righteousness and fame.
translations.idiomatic: ” Ying replied, “At the end of Yuanjia the succession was unsettled; the Grand Marshal gave his life to prove his loyalty, and the Minister over the Masses bore the burden of the realm—there was no saving himself—so he faced every peril for duty and honor.

sentences.zh: 今嗣主昏虐，狎近羣小，親賢誅戮，君子道消，外難屢作，曾無悛改。

translations.literal: Now the successor lord is benighted and cruel, intimate with petty men, executing kin and worthies; the way of the gentleman has faded; external troubles arise again and again, yet there has never been repentance.
translations.idiomatic: Today the heir is cruel and benighted, fond of petty men, slaying kin and worthies; the way of the gentleman has waned, troubles multiply from without, and he will not mend his ways.

sentences.zh: 今荊、雍協舉，乘據上流，背昏向明，勢無不濟。

translations.literal: Now Jing and Yong rise together, holding the upper reaches of the river; turning from darkness toward light, the momentum cannot fail to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Now Jing and Yong have risen together, holding the upper Yangzi; turning from darkness to light, their cause cannot fail.

sentences.zh: 百姓思治，天人之意可知；

translations.literal: The people long for order; the intent of Heaven and man can be known;
translations.idiomatic: The people yearn for peace—the will of Heaven and of men is plain;

sentences.zh: 旣明且哲，忠孝之途無爽。

translations.literal: being both bright and wise, the path of loyalty and filial piety is without error.
translations.idiomatic: to be clear-sighted and wise is to keep the path of loyalty and filial piety unclouded.

sentences.zh: 願明府更當雅慮，無祇悔也。

translations.literal: May Your Excellency reconsider with refined deliberation and not come to regret only afterward.
translations.idiomatic: May Your Excellency weigh this carefully and not repent too late.

sentences.zh: 」尋以公事免。

translations.literal: ” Soon he was dismissed on public grounds.
translations.idiomatic: ” Soon after he was removed from office on official grounds.

sentences.zh: 天監初，除征虜鄱陽王參軍，建安王中權錄事參軍，領軍長史，烏程令。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian he was appointed staff officer to the Pacification General Prince of Poyang, recording officer on the staff of the Central Guard of Prince Jian’an, chief clerk of the Army Director, and magistrate of Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianjian he became staff officer to the Pacification General Prince of Poyang, recording officer on Prince Jian’an’s Central Guard staff, chief clerk of the Army Director, and magistrate of Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 所受俸祿，悉歸于兄。

translations.literal: All salary he received he gave entirely to his elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Every stipend he received he turned over to his brother.

sentences.zh: 復爲臨川王錄事參軍，南臺治書，安成王錄事，太子翊軍校尉，累遷中散大夫、光祿卿，太中大夫。

translations.literal: He again served as recording officer on the staff of the Prince of Linchuan, drafting documents for the Southern Office, recording officer to the Prince of Ancheng, and Commandant of the Heir Apparent’s Guard; he was promoted in succession to Palace Gentleman, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as recording officer to the Prince of Linchuan, drafter for the Southern Office, recording officer to the Prince of Ancheng, and Commandant of the Heir Apparent’s Guard, rising through Palace Gentleman, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 大同五年，卒，年八十三。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Datong he died at the age of eighty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong year 5 he died, aged eighty-three.

sentences.zh: 子弘。

translations.literal: His son was Hong.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Hong.

sentences.zh: 蕭琛字彥瑜，蘭陵人。

translations.literal: Xiao Chen, courtesy name Yanyu, was a native of Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Chen, styled Yanyu, came from Lanling.

sentences.zh: 祖僧珍，宋廷尉卿。

translations.literal: His grandfather Sengzhen was Director of Justice under Song.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Sengzhen had been Director of Justice under the Song.

sentences.zh: 父惠訓，太中大夫。

translations.literal: His father Huixun was Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: His father Huixun had been Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 琛年數歲，從伯惠開撫其背曰：「必興吾宗。」

translations.literal: When Chen was several years old, his paternal uncle Huikai stroked his back and said, “You will surely revive our clan.”
translations.idiomatic: When Chen was still a child, his uncle Huikai stroked his back and said, “You will surely raise up our house.”

sentences.zh: 琛少而朗悟，有縱橫才辯。

translations.literal: Chen in youth was bright and perceptive, with talent for free-ranging debate.
translations.idiomatic: Chen was quick-witted from youth and possessed a debater’s eloquence.

sentences.zh: 起家齊太學博士。

translations.literal: He first entered office as Erudite of the Qi Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as Erudite of the Qi Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 時王儉當朝，琛年少，未爲儉所識，負其才氣，欲候儉。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Jian held the court; Chen was young and had not yet been noticed by Jian; relying on his talent and spirit, he wished to wait upon Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian then dominated the court; Chen was young and unknown to him, but confident in his gifts and determined to seek him out.

sentences.zh: 時儉宴于樂游苑，琛乃著虎皮靴，策桃枝杖，直造儉坐，儉與語，大悅。

translations.literal: When Jian was feasting in the Leyou Gardens, Chen put on tiger-skin boots, took a peach-branch staff, and went straight to Jian’s seat; Jian spoke with him and was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When Jian was feasting in the Leyou Gardens, Chen appeared in tiger-skin boots, leaning on a peach-branch staff, and walked straight to Jian’s seat; Jian spoke with him and was delighted.

sentences.zh: 儉爲丹陽尹，辟爲主簿，舉爲南徐州秀才，累遷司徒記室。

translations.literal: When Jian became Governor of Danyang he appointed Chen chief clerk, recommended him as the distinguished graduate of southern Xu, and promoted him in succession to recorder on the Grand Tutor’s staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Jian became governor of Danyang he made Chen his chief clerk, nominated him as southern Xu’s distinguished graduate, and promoted him to recorder on the Grand Tutor’s staff.

sentences.zh: 永明九年，魏始通好，琛再銜命到桑乾，還爲通直散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Yongming Wei first opened friendly relations; Chen twice bore the imperial commission to Sanggan and on his return became Regular Attendant of Direct Communication.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming year 9, when Wei first opened friendly relations, Chen twice carried the imperial commission to Sanggan; on his return he became Regular Attendant of Direct Communication.

sentences.zh: 時魏遣李道固來使，齊帝宴之。

translations.literal: At the time Wei sent Li Daogu as envoy, and the Qi emperor gave him a banquet.
translations.idiomatic: Wei then sent Li Daogu as envoy, and the Qi emperor entertained him at court.

sentences.zh: 琛於御筵舉酒勸道固，道固不受，曰：「公庭無私禮，不容受勸。

translations.literal: At the imperial banquet Chen raised his cup to urge Daogu to drink; Daogu would not accept, saying, “In the public court there is no private courtesy; I cannot accept urging to drink.
translations.idiomatic: At the imperial banquet Chen offered wine to Daogu; Daogu refused, saying, “At court there is no private courtesy—I cannot accept a personal toast.

sentences.zh: 」琛徐答曰：「《詩》所謂『雨我公田，遂及我私』。

translations.literal: ” Chen answered calmly, “As the Book of Songs says, ‘Rain on our public fields, and it reaches our private ones too.’
translations.idiomatic: ” Chen answered calmly, “As the Book of Songs says: ‘Rain on our public fields, and it reaches our private ones as well.’

sentences.zh: 」座者皆服，道固乃受琛酒。

translations.literal: ” All present were convinced, and Daogu then accepted Chen’s wine.
translations.idiomatic: ” The assembly was won over, and Daogu drank Chen’s toast.

sentences.zh: 遷司徒右長史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Chief Clerk of the Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Right Chief Clerk of the Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 出爲晉熙王長史、行南徐州事。

translations.literal: He went out as chief clerk to the Prince of Jinxi and acted for the southern Xu region.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as chief clerk to the Prince of Jinxi with charge of southern Xu.

sentences.zh: 還兼少府卿、尚書左丞。

translations.literal: On his return he concurrently served as Minister of the Lesser Treasury and Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On returning he also served as Minister of the Lesser Treasury and Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 始琛在宣城，有北僧南度，惟賚一葫蘆，中有《漢書序傳》。

translations.literal: When Chen was first at Xuancheng, a northern monk came south bearing only a gourd, within which was the “Ordered Biographies” of the Book of Han.
translations.idiomatic: While Chen was at Xuancheng, a northern monk came south carrying only a gourd that held the “Ordered Biographies” of the Book of Han.

sentences.zh: 僧曰：「三輔舊老相傳，以爲班固真本。

translations.literal: The monk said, “Old men of the Three Metropolises transmit that this is Ban Gu’s authentic version.
translations.idiomatic: The monk said, “Elders of the Three Metropolises have handed down that this is Ban Gu’s authentic text.

sentences.zh: 」琛固求得之，其書多有異今者，而紙墨亦古，文字多如龍舉之例，非隸非篆，琛甚秘之。

translations.literal: ” Chen pressed to obtain it; the book differed in many places from present versions, and the paper and ink were also ancient; the characters were mostly of the type called “dragon raised,” neither clerical nor seal script. Chen kept it very secret.
translations.idiomatic: ” Chen insisted on obtaining it; the text differed in many places from current versions, the paper and ink were ancient, and the script was mostly of the “dragon-raised” type—neither clerical nor seal. Chen guarded it closely.

sentences.zh: 及是行也，以書饟鄱陽王範，範乃獻于東宮。

translations.literal: On this mission he presented the book to the Prince of Poyang, Fan, and Fan then offered it to the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On this embassy he presented the book to Prince Fan of Poyang, who in turn offered it to the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 琛尋遷安西長史、南郡太守，母憂去官，又丁父艱。

translations.literal: Soon Chen was transferred to chief clerk of the Pacification West and Administrator of Nan Commandery; he left office for his mother’s mourning and again observed his father’s mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Chen was made chief clerk of the Pacification West and administrator of Nan Commandery; he left office for his mother’s death and again for his father’s.

sentences.zh: 起爲信武將軍、護軍長史，俄爲貞毅將軍、太尉長史。

translations.literal: He returned to office as Trustworthy Martial General and chief clerk of the Protector-General; soon he became Upright and Resolute General and chief clerk to the Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He returned as Trustworthy Martial General and chief clerk of the Protector-General, and soon became Upright and Resolute General and chief clerk to the Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 出爲信威將軍、東陽太守，遷吳興太守。

translations.literal: He went out as Trustworthy and Awesome General and Administrator of Dongyang, then was transferred to Administrator of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Trustworthy and Awesome General and administrator of Dongyang, then transferred to administrator of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 郡有項羽廟，土民名爲憤王，甚有靈驗，遂於郡廳事安施床幕爲神座，公私請禱，前後二千石皆於廳拜祠，而避居他室。

translations.literal: The commandery had a temple to Xiang Yu, whom the local people called the Wrathful King; it was very efficacious, and so in the main hall of the prefectural residence they had set up bed curtains as a spirit seat; public and private persons came to pray; former and later administrators of two thousand bushels all worshipped in the hall and lived elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery had a temple to Xiang Yu, whom locals called the Wrathful King and held in great awe; bed and curtains had been installed in the main hall as a spirit seat, and all who came to pray did so there—successive administrators worshipped in the hall and slept elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 琛至，徙神還廟，處之不疑。

translations.literal: When Chen arrived he moved the spirit back to the temple and took up residence without hesitation.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen arrived he returned the shrine to the temple and occupied the hall without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 又禁殺牛解祀，以脯代肉。

translations.literal: He also forbade killing cattle for sacrificial offerings, using dried meat in place of fresh.
translations.idiomatic: He also forbade cattle sacrifice, substituting dried meat for fresh offerings.

sentences.zh: 高祖在西邸，早與琛狎，每朝宴，接以舊恩，呼爲宗老。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor was in the Western Quarters he had long been intimate with Chen; at every court banquet he received him with old favor and called him “elder of the clan.”
translations.idiomatic: When the High Ancestor was still in the Western Quarters he had long been close to Chen; at court banquets he treated him with old affection and called him “clan elder.”

sentences.zh: 琛亦奉陳昔恩，以「早簉中陽，夙忝同閈，雖迷興運，猶荷洪慈。

translations.literal: Chen also offered thanks for past kindness, saying, “Long ago I took my place at Zhongyang; from of old I have been honored to share your gate; though I lost my way in the rise of fortune, I still bear your great kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Chen also voiced his gratitude for past kindness: “Long ago I stood in your company at Zhongyang; from the first I was honored to share your household; though I strayed when fortune turned, I still owe your great grace.

sentences.zh: 」上答曰：「雖云早契闊，乃自非同志；

translations.literal: ” The emperor answered, “Though you speak of an early bond, we were never truly of one mind;
translations.idiomatic: ” The emperor replied, “You speak of an early bond, yet we were never truly kindred spirits;

sentences.zh: 勿談興運初，且道狂奴異。」

translations.literal: do not speak of the beginning of the rise of fortune—rather tell how the mad servant was strange.”
translations.idiomatic: say nothing of how fortune began—tell instead how the mad servant was unlike the rest.”

sentences.zh: 琛常言：「少壯三好，音律、書、酒。

translations.literal: Chen often said, “In youth and vigor I had three loves: music, books, and wine.
translations.idiomatic: Chen often said, “In my prime I had three loves—music, books, and wine.

sentences.zh: 年長以來，二事都廢，惟書籍不衰。

translations.literal: Since growing older I have abandoned two of them; only books have not declined.
translations.idiomatic: As I have grown older I have given up two; only books have not faded.

sentences.zh: 」而琛性通脫，常自解竈，事畢餕餘，必陶然致醉。

translations.literal: ” Yet Chen’s nature was free and easy; he would often cook for himself, and when the meal was done and leftovers remained he would invariably grow pleasantly drunk.
translations.idiomatic: ” Yet Chen was free-spirited by nature; he often cooked for himself, and when the meal was done he would invariably drink himself into cheerful intoxication.

sentences.zh: 陸杲字明霞，吳郡吳人。

translations.literal: Lu Gao, courtesy name Mingxia, was a native of Wu in Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Gao, styled Mingxia, came from Wu in Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖徽，宋輔國將軍、益州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Hui was General Who Assists the State and Inspector of Yi Province under Song.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Hui had been General Who Assists the State and inspector of Yi Province under the Song.

sentences.zh: 父叡，揚州治中。

translations.literal: His father Rui was aide of Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: His father Rui had been chief aide of Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 杲性婞直，無所顧望。

translations.literal: Gao’s nature was upright and unyielding; he looked to nothing in fear.
translations.idiomatic: Gao was upright and unyielding, bowing to no one’s favor.

sentences.zh: 山陰令虞肩在任，贓污數百萬，杲奏收治。

translations.literal: Yu Jian, magistrate of Shanyin, while in office had embezzled several million; Gao memorialized to have him arrested and tried.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jian, magistrate of Shanyin, had embezzled millions while in office; Gao memorialized for his arrest and trial.

sentences.zh: 中書舍人黃睦之以肩事託杲，杲不答。

translations.literal: Huang Muzhi, Secretariat Attendant, asked Gao to intervene in Jian’s case; Gao did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Muzhi, a Secretariat Attendant, asked Gao to intervene in Jian’s case; Gao gave no answer.

sentences.zh: 高祖聞之，以問杲，杲答曰「有之」。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor heard of this he questioned Gao; Gao answered, “It is so.”
translations.idiomatic: When the High Ancestor heard of this he questioned Gao, who answered, “That is so.”

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「卿識睦之不？

translations.literal: The High Ancestor said, “Do you know Muzhi?
translations.idiomatic: The High Ancestor asked, “Do you know Muzhi?

sentences.zh: 」杲答曰：「臣不識其人。

translations.literal: ” Gao answered, “Your servant does not know the man.”
translations.idiomatic: ” Gao replied, “I do not know the man.”

sentences.zh: 」時睦之在御側，上指示杲曰：「此人是也。

translations.literal: ” At the time Muzhi was at the emperor’s side; the emperor pointed him out to Gao and said, “This is the man.”
translations.idiomatic: ” Muzhi was then at the emperor’s side; the emperor pointed and said, “This is he.”

sentences.zh: 」杲謂睦之曰：「君小人，何敢以罪人屬南司？

translations.literal: ” Gao said to Muzhi, “Sir, you are a petty man—how dare you entrust a criminal to the Southern Office?
translations.idiomatic: ” Gao said to Muzhi, “You petty fellow—how dare you hand a criminal over to the censorate?

sentences.zh: 」睦之失色。

translations.literal: ” Muzhi turned pale.
translations.idiomatic: ” Muzhi turned pale.

sentences.zh: 領軍將軍張稷，是杲從舅，杲嘗以公事彈稷，稷因侍宴訴高祖曰：「陸杲是臣通親，小事彈臣不貸。

translations.literal: The Army Director Zhang Ji was Gao’s maternal uncle; Gao once impeached Ji on public grounds. At a banquet Ji complained to the High Ancestor, saying, “Lu Gao is my close kin by marriage; on a trifling matter he impeached me and would not spare me.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ji, the Army Director, was Gao’s maternal uncle; Gao once impeached him on official grounds. At a banquet Ji complained to the High Ancestor: “Lu Gao is my close kinsman by marriage—over a trifle he impeached me and would show no mercy.

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「杲職司其事，卿何得爲嫌！

translations.literal: ” The High Ancestor said, “Gao’s office charged him with this duty—how can you hold a grudge!
translations.idiomatic: ” The High Ancestor said, “Gao was doing his duty—how can you resent it!

sentences.zh: 」杲在臺，號稱不畏強禦。

translations.literal: ” At the Censorate Gao was known as one who did not fear the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: ” At the Censorate Gao was known as one who did not fear the powerful.

sentences.zh: 六年，遷秘書監，頃之爲太子中庶子、光祿卿。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to Director of the Secretariat; soon after he became Palace Companion to the Heir Apparent and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 he became Director of the Secretariat; soon after he was made Palace Companion to the Heir Apparent and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 八年，出爲義興太守，在郡寬惠，爲民下所稱。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he went out as Administrator of Yixing; in the commandery he was lenient and kind and was praised by the people.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 he was sent out as administrator of Yixing, where his lenient and kindly rule won praise from the people.

sentences.zh: 還爲司空臨川王長史、領揚州大中正。

translations.literal: On his return he became chief clerk to the Minister of Works, Prince of Linchuan, and chief arbiter of Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: On returning he became chief clerk to the Minister of Works, Prince of Linchuan, and chief arbiter of Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 十四年，遷通直散騎侍郎，俄遷散騎常侍，中正如故。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was transferred to Regular Attendant of Direct Communication; soon he was transferred to Regular Attendant, retaining his post as chief arbiter.
translations.idiomatic: In year 14 he became Regular Attendant of Direct Communication, then soon Regular Attendant, keeping his arbiter’s post.

sentences.zh: 十五年，遷司徒左長史。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was transferred to Left Chief Clerk of the Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In year 15 he was made Left Chief Clerk of the Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 十六年，入爲左民尚書，遷太常卿。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he entered as Minister of the Left People and was transferred to Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: In year 16 he returned as Minister of the Left People, then became Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 普通二年，出爲仁威將軍、臨川內史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Putong he went out as Benevolent Martial General and Interior Secretary of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: In Putong year 2 he was sent out as Benevolent Martial General and interior secretary of Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 五年，入爲金紫光祿大夫，又領揚州大中正。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he entered as Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon and again held the chief arbiter’s post for Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5 he returned as Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon and again served as chief arbiter of Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 中大通元年，加特進，中正如故。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongdatong he was given the special advancement, retaining his post as chief arbiter.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhongdatong year 1 he received special advancement while keeping his arbiter’s post.

sentences.zh: 四年，卒，時年七十四。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died at the age of seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he died, aged seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 諡曰質子。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Zhizi.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Zhizi, “the Plain.”

sentences.zh: 杲素信佛法，持戒甚精，著《沙門傳》三十卷。

translations.literal: Gao had long believed in the Buddhist Law, kept the precepts with great precision, and authored the Biographies of Monks in thirty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Gao had long been a devout Buddhist, observed the precepts with great rigor, and wrote the Biographies of Monks in thirty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 弟煦，學涉有思理。

translations.literal: His younger brother Xu was learned and possessed reflective understanding.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Xu was learned and thoughtful.

sentences.zh: 天監初，歷中書侍郎，尚書左丞，太子家令，卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian he served in succession as Gentleman of the Secretariat, Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Director of the Heir Apparent’s Household, then died.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianjian he served as Gentleman of the Secretariat, Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Director of the Heir Apparent’s Household, then died.

sentences.zh: 撰《晉書》未就。

translations.literal: He was compiling a Book of Jin but did not complete it.
translations.idiomatic: He had begun a Book of Jin but did not finish it.

sentences.zh: 又著《陸史》十五卷，《陸氏驪泉志》一卷，並行於世。

translations.literal: He also authored the History of Lu in fifteen scrolls and the Record of the Lu Clan at Lichuan in one scroll; both circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote the History of Lu in fifteen scrolls and the Record of the Lu Clan at Lichuan in one scroll; both circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 子罩，少篤學，有文才，仕至太子中庶子、光祿卿。

translations.literal: His son Zhao from youth was devoted to learning, possessed literary talent, and rose in office to Palace Companion to the Heir Apparent and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhao was studious from youth and gifted in letters, rising to Palace Companion to the Heir Apparent and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：范岫、傅昭，並篤行清慎，善始令終，斯石建、石慶之徒矣。

translations.literal: The historian says: Fan Xiu and Fu Zhao alike were steadfast in conduct, pure and cautious, good in beginning and excellent in end—men of the type of Shi Jian and Shi Qing.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Fan Xiu and Fu Zhao were alike in steadfast conduct, purity, and caution, admirable from first to last—men in the mold of Shi Jian and Shi Qing.

sentences.zh: 蕭琛、陸杲俱以才學著名。

translations.literal: Xiao Chen and Lu Gao were both famed for talent and learning.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Chen and Lu Gao were both renowned for talent and learning.

sentences.zh: 琛朗悟辯捷，加諳究朝典，高祖在田，與琛遊舊，及踐天曆，任遇甚隆，美矣。

translations.literal: Chen was bright, perceptive, and quick in debate, and moreover thoroughly versed in court regulations; when the High Ancestor was still in the fields he had old ties of travel with Chen, and when he ascended the heavenly succession his favor and appointment were very lofty—beautiful indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Chen was quick-witted and eloquent and thoroughly versed in court precedent; the High Ancestor had known him in private life, and when he took the throne his favor was lavish—a fine thing indeed.

sentences.zh: 杲性婞直，無所忌憚，旣而執法憲臺，糾繩不避權幸，可謂允茲正色。

translations.literal: Gao’s nature was upright and unyielding, without dread; thereafter, wielding the law at the Censorate, he corrected and bound without avoiding the powerful and favored—one may say he truly bore the upright countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Gao was upright and fearless; at the Censorate he enforced the law without sparing the powerful—truly he wore the face of justice.

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：「彼己之子，邦之司直。

translations.literal: The Book of Songs says, “That other man—he is the upright judge of the state.”
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Songs says, “That man—he is the state’s upright judge.”

sentences.zh: 」杲其有焉。

translations.literal: ” In this Gao had his share.
translations.idiomatic: ” In this, Gao surely had his part.

translations.literal: [1] Endnote marker.
translations.idiomatic: [1] Endnote marker.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七三年五月版《梁書》爲本校。

translations.idiomatic: The full text has been collated against the Zhonghua Shuju, May 1973 edition of the 《Book of Liang》.
